title: Kanamycin (historical injectable)
dek: Kanamycin is a retired preferred DR-TB drug. eis promoter-up is its genomic signature. Ototoxicity did not retire when the guideline did; do not resurrect KM because a 2012 paper said XDR.
story: Kanamycin was a Group 2 injectable in the MDR era that defined old XDR (MDR + FQ + injectable). WHO removed injectables from preferred regimens because they maim hearing and kidneys without enough outcome gain once BDQ/LZD/FQ orals exist. KM is now salvage/Group C-adjacent history.

Resistance: eis promoter-up (low-level KM, often AMK-S), rrs 1401 (high-level KM+AMK±CAP), rare other rrs. WhiB7 overexpression phenocopies eis-up. Do not treat KM as interchangeable with AMK on a report.
If a programme still has KM vials, the ethical default is to prefer AMK only when an injectable is truly last-line, and to prefer not injecting. Audiometry is not optional nostalgia.
deep: A 2015 “XDR” isolate that is FQ-R + KM-R + BDQ-S + LZD-S is pre-XDR in 2021 language, not 2021-XDR.
Capreomycin is not a kinder KM.
Streptomycin is not KM. gidB does not answer this plate.

visual.caption: Schematic KM MIC: WT, eis promoter-up (modest right shift), rrs 1401 (large shift). AMK does not always follow the eis curve.

steps.body: The harm may already be done.

example.takeaway: Kanamycin is history plus ototoxicity. eis-up is not 2021-XDR.
